A 24-year-old female patient comes in for her yearly physical examination, stating she has no health
concerns to report. Her medical history includes major depressive disorder treated with sertraline. Her
vital signs show: temperature 99.4°F (37°C), blood pressure 102/68 mmHg, pulse 86/min, and
respirations 18/min. Physical examination reveals multiple bruises at various healing stages on her
upper arms, upper legs, and back, along with small circular lesions on her hips and stomach. When
questioned about these findings, she avoids eye contact and dismisses them, stating she is "just
clumsy" and "always tripping." What is the most appropriate initial response in this situation? Answer
Choices: (A) "Is someone hurting you?" (B) "I'm concerned about your safety at home." (C) "I need to
report this to the authorities immediately." (D) "Would you like to speak with a counselor today?" (E)
"Tell me more about what has been happening." (F) "Are you experiencing any bleeding disorders?"
(G) "Would you like me to examine these bruises more closely?" (H) "Do you have a safe place to go if
things get out of hand?" (I) "These bruises don't look like they're from falling." (J) "I can call the police
so that they can protect you."
 A. "Tell me more about what has been happening."
B. "Would you like me to examine these bruises more closely?"
C. "I need to report this to the authorities immediately."
D. "Is someone hurting you?"
E. "These bruises don't look like they're from falling."
F. "Are you experiencing any bleeding disorders?"
G. "I'm concerned about your safety at home."
H. "I can call the police so that they can protect you."
I. "Would you like to speak with a counselor today?"
J. "Do you have a safe place to go if things get out of hand?"
